SMTO-EXE-0130 — SMTO lost contact with the web browser on your Gateway

GUID: 395ba619-a2b2-5814-94b1-ea506190a3b5
Slug: browser-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach the Gateway, the helper program that runs the web browser for SMTO, or that Gateway was shutting down. The browser step got no answer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on, awake and connected to the network. Browser steps run on that computer, so SMTO can't reach the browser while it is off, asleep or offline.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. This confirms SMTO can reach the Gateway again before you continue the task.
  3. Once it shows Connected, ask SMTO to look at the current page before repeating the step. If the Gateway restarted, ask SMTO to open the website again. Browser windows close when the Gateway restarts, and a fresh look shows whether your last click or form already went through.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as Connected, and SMTO can open and describe the web page again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to resubmit a form or payment until you've checked on the website that it didn't already go through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A browser call to the selected Gateway failed at the connection level (HTTP or outbound connection error, a failed cancel request, or the Gateway's browser service was already shut down).

What this means

  • Browser transport received an HTTP or other Gateway error, cancellation failed, or the browser service loop was already closed. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser transport received an HTTP or other Gateway error, cancellation failed, or the browser service loop was already closed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect failure phase, HTTP status, service lifecycle and the original action's effect flag; distinguish admission rejection from response loss.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's status in Settings › Setup › Gateways and the Gateway log for shutdown or connection errors around the failure. Restore connectivity and refresh Gateway metadata, then inspect state with browser.sessions and browser.page_info before repeating; managed browser sessions do not survive a Gateway restart.
  • Restore the selected Gateway connection and refresh metadata. Check effect_unknown before repeating the operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restore the selected Gateway connection and refresh metadata. Check effect_unknown before repeating the operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended service is available and the original browser action is settled before new work.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
